incident.observed: A newly opened /wc chat returned the exact historical completion for worker wc-20260918T212321Z-94fec87501.
incident.truth_boundary: The text matched durable historical evidence, but no new beacon/worker identity was created for the new human launch. Historical truth was replayed as if it were current execution.

invariant: Every canonical human /w or /wc invocation is a NEW worker launch unless the human explicitly names an existing worker_id and asks to resume it. New launches may never adopt a worker_id from memory, prior chats, model context, repository examples, runtime, scoreboard, receipts, exams or no-allocation artifacts.

fresh_identity.generation: Generate current UTC timestamp plus a de-novo 12-hex suffix in this turn. Never copy the suffix or whole worker_id from any observed artifact.
fresh_identity.atomic_uniqueness_gate: CREATE coordination/workers/beacons/<worker_id>.json before frontier allocation. Never pre-read the candidate beacon path.
fresh_identity.create_exists: If beacon CREATE returns CREATE_EXISTS, discard the worker_id completely, generate a new suffix and retry beacon CREATE, maximum 3 total beacon identity attempts.

beacon_values.source: surface that created the beacon: /w for stable production, /wc for canary/RUN
beacon_values.launch_nonce: fresh de-novo 16hex generated in this turn; must not be copied from prior artifacts

replay_guards: Existing exam/RETURN/no-allocation/CLOSE evidence for any other worker_id is historical evidence only and can never satisfy the current launch.
A current launch cannot emit a terminal human response before its own fresh beacon CREATE succeeded.
For v3.30 terminal exams, launch_nonce must equal the current beacon launch_nonce.
If a worker cannot create a fresh beacon after the bounded identity attempts, close as FRESH_LAUNCH_BEACON_NOT_CREATED. It must not summarize or present a historical worker as the current result.
A worker may resume an old worker_id only when the HUMAN MESSAGE explicitly names that exact worker_id and explicitly requests resume/recovery.

smoke_gate.pass_when: 3 distinct v3.30 beacons exist from post-fix guarded human launches; none reuse a prior worker_id; any explicit v3.30 exam matches its beacon launch_nonce. Each launch remains an ordinary resident PROD-01 worker and continues toward target 6 unless a real boundary/exhaustion is proven.

human_inline_launch_guard.reason: The replay incident occurred before a new worker beacon existed; repository/page-only anti-replay text is too late if a chat answers from historical project/model context without dereferencing the launcher.
required_markers: PROHIBIDO reutilizar identidad o resultado histórico
RESIDENTE_POOL: 3=checkpoint, objetivo=6, tope=8 salvo boundary real
human_inline_launch_guard.rule: A Guide must hand the human the exact guarded active invocation. /w or /wc receiving NUEVO_WORKER=1 treats the message as a fresh launch envelope before consulting historical worker evidence. CONTINUIDAD_RESIDENTE=1 makes RETURN→E8/SUBMIT_NEXT the default nonterminal transition; below-target close still requires a real durable boundary or fresh compatible-frontier exhaustion. Finite measured waves additionally preserve BATCH/EXPECTED in the first beacon.
human_inline_launch_guard.durable_truth: The inline marker does not itself prove launch success; only this turn's own fresh beacon does.

productive_smoke.rule: Fresh launches are ordinary full PROD-01 resident workers, not verification-only/no-op probes. Beacon creation and one completed job do not terminate work; after each nonterminal RETURN the worker proceeds directly to E8/SUBMIT_NEXT. Below target, only a real durable boundary or freshly proven compatible-frontier exhaustion permits close.

forms.batch: BATCH <batch_id> EXPECTED <n> => preserve exact batch_id and positive integer expected_workers; pool_id=null
forms.canary_resident_pool_alias: On source=/wc only: RESIDENTE_POOL present with no explicit RUN/BATCH/POOL identity => launch_class=POOL, batch_id=POOL-PROD-01, expected_workers=null, pool_id=PROD-01
forms.unbatched: otherwise, after evaluating the canary resident-pool alias, batch_id=UNBATCHED, expected_workers=null, pool_id=null

canary_resident_pool_alias.trigger: RESIDENTE_POOL is present AND no explicit RUN <run_id>, BATCH <batch_id> EXPECTED <n>, or POOL <pool_id> identity is present
canary_resident_pool_alias.reason: Resident canary launches were arriving with pool residency semantics but no explicit POOL token, becoming UNBATCHED and therefore losing deterministic pooled sharding and POOL_TAIL_RESCUE. The alias repairs classification without adding a scheduler, queue or authority layer.

launch_envelope.downstream_predicate_rule: All downstream /wc protocol predicates written as BATCH/POOL invocation, POOL-only, pooled worker, batch/pool sharding, or POOL_TAIL_RESCUE MUST evaluate the parsed launch_class and persisted beacon identity from this parser rather than re-parsing literal human tokens. Therefore a canary_resident_pool_alias launch is pool-classified for sharding/residency/tail-rescue. This rule does not alter /w explicit-envelope parsing.
launch_envelope.first_beacon_rule: The surface creating the first beacon must persist parsed batch_id, expected_workers and pool_id in that beacon before loading any mutable repo state.
launch_envelope.refill_rule: A finite BATCH is complete when durable runtime observed workers reaches expected_workers. If fewer are observed, Guide requests exactly missing_expected fresh launches using the identical BATCH prompt. Existing batch workers are never relaunched/recounted.
launch_envelope.no_inference: No cause may be inferred for a human wake that produced no durable beacon.
